english_verification.review_scope: Read the complete B24 source body and original evidence page; checked current country history, representative mission and English narrative terms for human-orc equality, half-orc community, warrior training, and Bladebreaker revenge. Read the exact local Wiki chunks for the clan's shamans and Arosha, the unfinished Greentide section, and its wisdom-first culture. No full mission audit. Primary compared all native idea names/descriptions by actual current English localisation key. Source ranges may be locator envelopes; conditional and predecessor idea sets remain separate. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The English Wiki's Greentide-history section explicitly says it is incomplete; no detailed campaign chronology is inferred from it.
Unguldavor is a possible later formable shared by eligible Orc countries, not a required or B24-exclusive formation.

rationale.campaign_length: 25 Clouded Eye-specific missions plus several shared Orc definitions; formation replaces the mission tree.
rationale.colonization: Settling in Escann is important, but overseas colonization is not a focus.
rationale.complexity: Reform, half-orc population, and formable-country conditions are connected.
rationale.dark_story: Revenge and the Greentide legacy cast a shadow, but the overall route trends toward equality.
rationale.difficulty: War and reform backlash must be managed together; not tested in an actual playthrough.
rationale.diplomacy: The mission narrative emphasizes negotiation and cross-cultural relations.
rationale.early_pressure: Several powers compete for land around the starting position.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Shamans and the Clouded Eye relic matter, but do not create a campaign-wide spellcasting loop.
rationale.narrative_density: Grama, Arosha, and Unguldavor form a story of succession.
rationale.tall_play: The Ardent Keep and urban institutions anchor the unique mission tree.
rationale.warfare: The opening requires fighting neighboring clans and human states.

identity.appearance: A Green Orc tribe in 1444, ruled by Grama; Arosha's route belongs to later missions.
identity.formation_scope: May form Unguldavor (Z52) through a general Orc decision; former B24 countries have a unique continuation condition, but the formation is not exclusive to B24.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Adopting new ideas depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: For generations our sagely shamans have sacrificed their very vision in an ancient clan ritual known as "The Trial of Clouded", all in the pursuit of Dookan’s wisdom. The ritual is a dangerous one, but those who survive find themselves better attuned with shamanic magics. A worthy few may even wield "The Clouded Eye", a mystical object consisting of a rough uncut gem of pure glowing white crystal. A treasure our clan has long guarded, the Eye is believed to have been gifted directly from Dookan and may even be the eye of the chained god himself. With the power to bestow great visions of a possible future and detail insights on the lore of the past, what other origin could there be?

description.text: While other clans may sing of bold and mighty warchiefs, we instead honor the wise and clever; none other embodies this better than our legendary chieftain, Grama. It was her prophetic dream of the verdant lands outside that led us to rally behind Korgus as one of his first and most fervent followers. It was her clever tongue that settled disputes between the clans as the Greentide swept from Castellyr to Farranaen, carving apart the old kingdoms of Escann. It was her guile at Rottenstep that left the Aldresians decimated under the might of our shamans. And when The Dookanson fell, it was she who led us to the rich hills of Gulenhyl where our people may bring life to the vision she had so many years ago. Even after she draws her final breath, we know that it will be her teachings that will guide us toward our new future.

description.text:
With the death of beloved Grama and the increasing pressure faced from the adventurer onslaught, our seers desperately scoured our clan for a leader, a new warchief who could lead us to glory and unite the clans torn asunder by Dookansfall. Yet as we divined the fates of our fiercest warriors and wisest shamans, despair began to set in. Every orc, from the descendants of Grama herself to the seasoned veterans of the Greentide, was doomed to meet their end by the adventurer's blade or by the slaver's chain.

Then she came.

 Clad in the armor reminiscent of our adventurer foes and mighty axe in hand, Arosha of the disgraced Oakbreakers would arrive in Clouded Eye to much commotion. After leaving any warrior who challenged her sprawled on the ground, Arosha called out to the shamans of our clan. With a bellow, the warrior gave voice to the lessons learned in her exile. Lessons from her once companion, Corin Korguskiller. That strength and honor were made whole by duty and compassion.

When Arosha had finished, the gathered shamans did not respond at first. Nor did they attempt to divine with magic or invoke the Clouded Eye. Instead, they kneeled. For the first time since Grama’s death, the future was clear. Ushering in the era of Arosha Oakbreaker, Chieftain of Clouded Eye.

description.text:
The decades after the Greentide’s ultimate defeat and Korgus Dookanson’s death would be a chaotic one for the Escanni orcs. For two decades, ultimate authority had been centralised around Korgus and his divine connection to Dookan. His downfall did not simply shatter orcish unity, it left a power vacuum within the clans themselves as many chieftains had tied their own legitimacy to Korgus’ (and by extension Dookan’s) will.

Roughly equivalent to the idiom of "ruling with an iron fist", Tuladosh, or steel hand, represented the various Escanni orcish chieftains bids to assert firmer control over their clans. Some would attempt to take up Korgus’ fallen mantle in a bid for legitimacy. Others would focus their efforts on rebuilding the ruined land to build trust. More still would settle for trying to dominate the local surroundings to show their strength. All would find their efforts a struggle.

description.text:
As the Green Orcs transitioned from conquerors to inhabitants, two classes would come to form within the various nascent kingdoms - the Dargom and Ozdan. Residing within the rebuilt hamlets and refounded towns, the Dargom represented the evolution of orcish society.

Dominated by craftspeople, merchants and other urban roles, the Dargom stemmed from those who already held great wealth and power or recognized the power that could come from craftsmanship and commerce. Through these means, the Dargom would form the basis of the nascent bureaucracy and come to control much of the state’s wealth.

The Ozdan, on the other hand, represented unchanging orcish tradition. Dominated by travelling warriors and migratory herders who were either too poor (or too stubborn) to settle, the Ozdan’s hearty lifestyle meant they were a natural pool to draw on for the kingdom’s defence. While capable, their adherence to the old ways would lead constant headaches to the central government

description.text:
While the animosity between the orcs of Escann and the other races would last generations as the struggle for land continued into the 16th century, old hatred would eventually give way to cold utilitarianism.

Heralding this evolution would be the Crimson Deluge, a seemingly divine cataclysm that showered Escann with blood and gore. With these unnatural events came disruptions to commerce as tumultuous weather began to claim Escanni caravans. As an economic crisis began to brew, it would be the orcish kingdoms who would step in. Orcs, stronger than the average human and born wayfinders, were more capable of withstanding the treacherous rains and the violence it wrought. While initially rejected, the merchants of Cannor found themselves more willing to look the other way and allow orcs to trek these treacherous routes as long as the coin flowed.

description.text:
Whatever equilibrium that arose between the adventurer kingdoms and orcish kingdoms would come to a violent end when the first witch kings arose. Armies onto themselves, the orcish kingdoms buckled under the likes of mages like Laurens síl Place and the Regent of Wyvernheart. When even the most powerful shamans were reduced to dust in the face of such foes, it was clear new tactics had to be adopted.

What came about was the sagah’dams, or shadowshots. Taking advantage of their skin’s natural camouflage in the greenery of Escann, these warriors would rely on ambush tactics to inhibit and blunt ever more brazen advances into orcish land. As these brave orcs fought to preserve their home, some could not help but find it ironic it was they who were now being swept away by some unstoppable tide…

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who want effortless plunder and have little patience for city-building or reform rebellions.
player_overview.how_it_plays: First secure a foothold and the Ardent Keep, then manage the city, half-orc population, and reforms; optionally form Unguldavor and handle the clan backlash.
player_overview.overview: Begin as an orcish shaman clan ruled by Grama, competing for land with old enemies in Escann while proving that orcs can survive through strategy, negotiation, and institutions. Arosha's route takes the clan toward the Ardent Keep, urban development, and a multi-ethnic society; the deeper the reforms go, the stronger the backlash from the old clans. You can eventually build Unguldavor with other Orcs, but that is a future the player must pursue, not the opening state.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy orcish reconstruction, a multi-ethnic state, and a continuous story from tribe to kingdom.
signature_features: Grama and Arosha's succession turn an Orc campaign into a story of reform.
The Ardent Keep, a half-orc community, and Dagom politics turn conquest toward urban governance.
The general Unguldavor formable preserves follow-up content for countries with a Clouded Eye past Tag.
player_overview.tagline: Lead Greentide remnants beyond the age of plunder and build a shared city for Orcs, half-orcs, and humans.

reasons: A clear turn toward Orc reform and half-orc equality.
City-building and tribal warfare run in parallel.
The Clouded Eye retains a continuation after forming Unguldavor.
warnings: A neighboring country may occupy the Ardent Keep first.
The reform route brings backlash from the old clans.

positive_indicators: Missions explicitly establish equality between Orcs and humans.
Half-orcs are no longer treated as non-persons.
Cities, bureaucracy, and safer military institutions serve residents.
values.rationale: There is strong positive evidence for half-orcs and humans living as equals, reducing pointless warrior deaths, and building cities; revenge against the Bladebreakers and repression during reform reduce restraint. War and orcish identity do not enter the good/evil score.
red_flags: The revenge text against the Bladebreakers uses language of destruction.
Dagom reforms provoke resistance from the old clans.
